intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots inside a protected marine sanctuary. Families can swim alongside colorful tropical fish and sea turtles in calm, shallow waters. Reservations are required in advance and an educational video is shown before entry.

experiences.name: Catamaran Sunset Sail off Waikiki
experiences.description: Board a family-friendly catamaran for a 2-hour sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Enjoy views of Diamond Head, spot dolphins and sea turtles, and experience the magic of a Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean. Light snacks and drinks are typically included.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove
experiences.description: Experience an authentic Hawaiian luau on the beach featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and haupia coconut pudding. A wonderful cultural immersion for the whole family right on the oceanfront.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming surf town of Haleiwa on the North Shore and sample Hawaii's most beloved food traditions. Try world-famous shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies — a delicious and affordable family food adventure.

experiences.name: Beginner Surf Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take a 2-hour group surf lesson with certified instructors on the gentle rolling waves of Waikiki, considered one of the best beginner surf spots in the world. Suitable for kids and adults alike, boards and rash guards are provided. Most first-timers stand up on their first lesson!

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots inside a protected marine sanctuary. Families can swim alongside colorful tropical fish and sea turtles in calm, shallow waters. Reservations are required in advance and an educational video is shown before entry.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up a TheBus day pass (~$3/person) or arrange a budget rideshare to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu (~30–40 min). Check in to the Boutique Stay, unpack, and freshen up. Take a short stroll along the neighborhood to get oriented and pick up snacks and groceries at a nearby Foodland or Times Supermarket to stock the room for budget breakfasts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Koko Marina Center for a casual, affordable dinner. Try Zippy's — a beloved local chain offering plate lunches and saimin from ~$8–12. Walk along the marina waterfront at sunset to decompress from travel.

meals.breakfast: Snacks on the plane or grab a granola bar from the airport convenience store
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick plate lunch from a food truck near the airport or a L&L Hawaiian Barbecue (~$10–13)
meals.dinner: Zippy's at Koko Marina Center — chili, plate lunches, or saimin bowls (~$8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a reusable water bottle and reef-safe sunscreen at the supermarket tonight — you'll need both daily. Download the TheBus app (DaBus2) for free route planning. Reserve your Hanauma Bay snorkeling entry online tonight for Day 2 — slots fill up fast and must be booked in advance ($25/adult, free under 12).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve (opens 6:45 AM — arrive by 7:00 AM to beat crowds). Watch the mandatory 9-minute marine education video, then snorkel the crystal-clear protected bay teeming with sea turtles, parrotfish, and reef fish. Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$12/set) or bring your own. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the shallow reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit Hanauma Bay by midday and walk or drive the short distance to the Halona Blowhole Lookout (free) — a dramatic lava shelf where ocean waves shoot water through a natural rock spout. Continue to Sandy Beach Park, one of Oahu's most scenic beaches. Note: Sandy Beach has strong shore break — ideal for watching bodyboarders but supervise children closely near the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rinse off and rest. Head to Koko Marina Center for dinner at Poke Stop or a local poke bowl counter — build-your-own bowls are fresh, filling, and budget-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at the hotel — cereal, fruit, or yogurt from yesterday's grocery run (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from home (sandwiches, fruit, chips) to eat at Hanauma Bay's picnic area, or buy a hot dog/snack at the bay's concession stand (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Poke Stop at Koko Marina (~$12–15 per person for a poke bowl with rice and toppings)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — confirm your booking from last night. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before entering the water (chemical sunscreens are banned in the bay). Parking at Hanauma Bay is $3/car or take TheBus Route 22 (Hanauma Bay Shuttle) for ~$3/person each way.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or bus to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (free) — a paved, 2-mile round-trip coastal hike with stunning panoramic views of the Windward Coast, sea cliffs, and the islands of Molokai and Lanai in the distance. From November to May humpback whales are visible; in August look for spinner dolphins offshore. The trail is stroller-accessible and great for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the Windward Coast via Kalanianaole Highway to Waimanalo Beach — consistently rated one of Oahu's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches with long white sand and calm turquoise water, perfect for families. Spend 2–3 hours swimming, building sandcastles, and relaxing. Stop at Keneke's BBQ in Waimanalo for a classic Hawaiian plate lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward East Oahu. Stop at the Koolau Mountains overlook on Pali Highway for a scenic twilight view. Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Self-prepare a simple dinner using groceries.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — toast, eggs, or oatmeal self-prepared (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Keneke's BBQ in Waimanalo — kalua pork plate, loco moco, or teriyaki chicken (~$10–13 per person)
meals.dinner: Self-prepared pasta or rice dish at the hotel (~$3–5 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Makapu'u trailhead parking is free but fills by 8 AM on weekends — Monday is typically less crowded. Bring plenty of water for the hike (no shade on the trail). Waimanalo Beach Park has restrooms, showers, and covered picnic tables.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus or drive into Honolulu (about 25–35 min from East Oahu) to visit Iolani Palace (self-guided audio tour ~$13/adult, ~$5/child 5–12) — the only royal palace on U.S. soil and a fascinating piece of Hawaiian history. Walk through the grounds and the neighboring Kawaiahao Church and Mission Houses for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Chinatown Honolulu — a vibrant, budget-friendly neighborhood perfect for families. Browse the open-air Oahu Market, explore lei shops, and grab lunch at the Chinatown Cultural Plaza food stalls. Afterward, stroll along the Honolulu waterfront and visit Aloha Tower Marketplace (free entry) for harbor views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Waikiki (short bus or drive from downtown) for an evening walk along Waikiki Beach to watch the sunset. Grab dinner at a budget spot on Kuhio Avenue away from the beachfront (prices drop significantly one block inland).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fruit, cereal, coffee (~$2–3 self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Chinatown food stalls or Mei Sum Dim Sum restaurant (~$8–11 per person for dim sum or noodle dishes)
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon noodles made in-house from ~$7–10 per person, very family-friendly

day_by_day.notes: Validate TheBus transfers to save money on multi-leg trips. Iolani Palace is closed on Sundays and Mondays — Wednesday is perfect. Chinatown can be eclectic; it's safe and interesting for families during daytime hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (parking $10/car or TheBus Route 23 + short walk). Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip crater trail with 560-foot elevation gain — offers sweeping 360° views of Honolulu and the Pacific. Trail takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip. Bring water and snacks. Reserve entry online in advance at gostateparks.hawaii.gov ($5/person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off at Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) just east of Waikiki — a quieter, locals-favorite beach with good snorkeling near the reef. Free parking and entry. Spend 2–3 hours here before heading back toward East Oahu.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Rainbow Drive-In on Kapahulu Avenue — a legendary Honolulu institution since 1961. Enjoy plate lunches, loco moco, and mixed plates at very affordable prices. Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the hike — banana, granola bar, coffee (~$2)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from the hotel eaten at Diamond Head or Kaimana Beach (~$3–5 self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Rainbow Drive-In — plate lunch, loco moco, or chili rice (~$9–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head trail can be hot and exposed — start by 8 AM if possible to avoid midday heat. The tunnel and spiral staircase sections are exciting for kids. Book Diamond Head entry online to guarantee access — walk-ins are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Drive up the Windward Coast to Kailua — about 25 minutes from Hanauma Bay via the Pali Highway. Visit Kailua Beach Park, consistently ranked among the best beaches in the U.S., with calm, clear turquoise water ideal for families. Arrive early to claim a shaded picnic spot. Swim, snorkel, or try stand-up paddleboarding (rental ~$20/hour from Kailua Beach Adventures).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kailua Town — a charming, walkable village with boutique shops, art galleries, and excellent local eateries. Browse Macy's Farmers Market (Thursdays and Sundays) or just stroll the town. Visit Lanikai Beach — a short drive or bike ride from Kailua — for one of the most photographed stretches of sand in Hawaii (free, street parking only).
day_by_day.evening: Return to East Oahu via the scenic Pali Highway. Stop at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout (~$3 parking) for dramatic valley and ocean views at golden hour. Dinner at a local spot near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — grab sandwiches, wraps, and cold drinks to enjoy on the beach (~$10–14 per person)
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood near East Honolulu — fresh poke bowls at local prices (~$12–15) or self-prepared dinner at the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has no public facilities — use Kailua Beach Park restrooms before heading over. Street parking at Lanikai is limited; arrive early or walk/bike from Kailua. The Pali Highway lookout is breezy and dramatic — bring a light layer for the kids.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu (adults ~$25, children 4–17 ~$17 — book online for slight discount) — the premier natural and cultural history museum of Hawaii and the Pacific. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, Science Adventure Center (kids love it), and planetarium. Plan 2.5–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Foster Botanical Garden in downtown Honolulu (adults $5, children 6–12 $1 — one of Oahu's best budget attractions). Walk among massive heritage trees, tropical blooms, and rare plant collections. Afterward, take a short walk to Nuuanu Avenue's art galleries for free browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Saturday Night KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (4:00–7:00 PM, free entry) — sample local food, fresh produce, Hawaiian snacks, and artisan goods. This is a fantastic and very affordable dinner option with food stalls offering everything from garlic shrimp to malasadas.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Café inside Bishop Museum or pack a lunch from the hotel (~$5–8 at café)
meals.dinner: KCC Saturday Farmers Market food stalls — graze on local foods: garlic shrimp, kalua pork sliders, fresh fruit, malasadas (~$10–15 per person total)

day_by_day.notes: The KCC Farmers Market is one of the best budget food experiences in Honolulu — arrive by 4:30 PM as popular vendors sell out. Bishop Museum is closed on Tuesdays; Saturday is a great day to visit. Combine with Foster Garden to maximize the day's cultural value.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the North Shore — about 1 hour drive from East Oahu via H-3 and H-2 or the scenic Kamehameha Highway. Stop at Waimea Bay Beach Park for a swim in the calm August waters (North Shore is calm in summer, big waves only in winter). The beach is stunning and free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Kamehameha Highway through Haleiwa Town — the surf culture capital of Oahu. Browse the surf shops, visit Matsumoto Shave Ice (a Hawaii institution — ~$4–6 per shave ice) and stroll the historic town. Head to Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach Park for more beautiful scenery and a relaxed afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward East Oahu via the H-2 and H-1 freeways. Stop at Ted's Bakery near Sunset Beach before leaving the North Shore — famous for chocolate haupia pie (~$5/slice) and plate lunches (~$11–14). Return to the hotel for a restful evening.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared hotel breakfast before the drive (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku — the original North Shore shrimp truck, garlic shrimp plate ~$14–16 (a must-do North Shore experience)
meals.dinner: Ted's Bakery plate lunch or early dinner (~$11–14) eaten at Sunset Beach before the drive home

day_by_day.notes: Rent a car for this day if relying on TheBus — the North Shore trip by bus takes 2+ hours each way and limits flexibility. Gas for a rental car split among a family is very cost-effective. Giovanni's Shrimp Truck has a long line — arrive before noon. Waimea Bay jumping rock (20-foot cliff jump into the bay) is popular with older kids and teens — parents should assess conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay for a second snorkeling session (re-use any gear you rented or bring your own this time). Focus on exploring the deeper Witches Brew channel if the family is comfortable — more diverse marine life including larger fish and sea turtles. Alternatively, spend a relaxed morning at nearby Koko Head District Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Koko Head Crater Trail (free) — a challenging but rewarding 1,048-step staircase built on old military railway tracks leading to panoramic summit views of East Oahu, Hanauma Bay, and Koko Crater. Suitable for older children and adults; takes about 45–60 minutes up. Skip if traveling with very young children and substitute with a beach afternoon at Koko Marina or Portlock Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final full evening near the hotel. Visit Koko Marina Sunset Cruise viewpoint (free) or simply walk the marina. Treat the family to shave ice or ice cream at a nearby shop. Self-prepare a simple farewell dinner at the hotel using remaining groceries.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel breakfast — use up remaining groceries (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Concession at Hanauma Bay or packed lunch on the beach (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Self-prepared farewell dinner at the hotel — grilled items, rice, salad (~$4–6 per person) plus shave ice or malasadas for dessert from a nearby shop (~$4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Koko Head Trail is steep with no shade — bring 2 liters of water per person and start before 9 AM to avoid heat. The steps are uneven in places; wear closed-toe shoes. This is a great final active day before a travel day tomorrow. Confirm flight details and pack tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — take one last walk along the East Oahu coastline near the hotel to soak in the views. Depending on flight time, visit a nearby beach for a final swim or simply enjoy coffee and breakfast with an ocean view. Check out of the hotel per checkout policy (typically 11 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport (Daniel K. Inouye International Airport, HNL) with ample time — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international or mainland flights. Stop at Longs Drugs or ABC Stores at the airport for last-minute Hawaiian snacks and souvenirs (macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, li hing mui candy) at better prices than airport gift shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with incredible memories. If the flight is delayed or there is extra time, grab a final meal at the airport's Makai Market Food Court in Terminal 2 — local options including poke, plate lunches, and saimin at reasonable airport prices (~$12–16).

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — use last of the groceries or treat the family to Leonard's Bakery malasadas if passing through Honolulu (~$1.50 each)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from the hotel or a quick stop at a grocery store deli near the airport (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport Makai Market Food Court — poke bowls, plate lunches, or saimin (~$12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: TheBus Route 20 or 31 connects Waikiki and East Honolulu to the airport for just $3/person — a great budget option if you have light luggage. Rideshare from East Oahu to the airport is typically $25–40. Return any rental car with a full tank to avoid surcharges. Hawaiian Airlines and Southwest both allow one free checked bag for Hawaiian routes — confirm your airline's policy.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up rental car, and drive ~25 minutes to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, unpack, and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach near Hanauma Bay to get your bearings and enjoy the ocean views. Grab a refreshing drink from a nearby café.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first night — enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant close to the hotel. Head to bed early to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport or on the plane before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up plate lunches from a local deli or grocery store (like Foodland) near the hotel — try the classic Hawaiian plate with kalua pork, rice, and mac salad (~$12–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Hawaii Kai (~10 min drive) — casual waterfront dining with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and local craft beers. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Purchase or reserve a timed entry reservation for Hanauma Bay online tonight for Day 2 — spots fill up fast. Reservations open 2 days in advance at 7:00 AM HST.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Watch the mandatory marine education video, rent snorkel gear on-site (~$12), and explore the protected coral reef teeming with sea turtles, colorful fish, and vibrant coral. Perfect for all family ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel to rinse off and relax. Head to nearby Koko Head Crater Trail for a scenic hike up 1,048 steps with panoramic views of East Oahu — moderate difficulty, great for older kids and adults (~1.5 hours round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hawaii Kai Marina area for a waterfront dinner, then enjoy a sunset walk along the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and pastries at a local café near the hotel before heading to Hanauma Bay.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from a grocery store to enjoy at the beach or picnic area at Hanauma Bay — no outside food allowed inside the bay itself, but there is a snack bar on-site.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood (Hawaii Kai area) or Roy's Hawaii Kai — Roy's is a mid-range splurge with excellent Hawaiian fusion cuisine. Budget ~$35–50 per person for Roy's; ~$15–20 for Ono Seafood.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay entry fee is $25 per adult (free for Hawaii residents and children under 13). Parking is $3. Sunscreen must be reef-safe — bring your own or purchase on-site. The bay closes on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Windward Coast — head north along the Pali Highway, stop at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for breathtaking views of the Ko'olau Mountains and Windward Oahu. Continue to Kailua Town, a charming beachside community with boutique shops and local eateries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kailua Beach Park, consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches. Crystal-clear turquoise water, calm waves, and white sand make it ideal for families. Rent kayaks (~$25–35/hour) to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Honolulu for the Catamaran Sunset Sail off Waikiki — board a family-friendly 2-hour sunset cruise along the iconic Waikiki coastline. Enjoy views of Diamond Head, dolphins, and a glowing Pacific sunset.

meals.breakfast: Morning Glory Café in Kailua — popular local spot with açaí bowls, eggs, and fresh-pressed juice. Budget ~$12–18 per person.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Café & Deli in Kailua — beloved local deli with fresh sandwiches, salads, and smoothies. Budget ~$12–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Enjoy light pupus (appetizers) and drinks on the catamaran, then grab dinner at a Waikiki restaurant post-cruise. Duke's Waikiki offers great beachfront dining with fresh fish and Hawaiian classics. Budget ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Catamaran Sunset Sail typically departs around 5:00–5:30 PM from Waikiki Beach. Book in advance. Drive from Kailua to Waikiki is about 25–30 minutes — plan accordingly. Tuesday is a good day for this since Hanauma Bay is closed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, royal regalia, volcanic geology exhibits, and a planetarium show. Excellent for families and highly educational. (~2–3 hours)
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Iolani Palace, the only royal palace on U.S. soil, for a guided tour. Learn about the Hawaiian monarchy and Queen Liliuokalani. Afterward, stroll through the historic downtown Honolulu waterfront and Chinatown.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove — experience an authentic Hawaiian luau on the beach featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performance, imu ceremony (underground oven), and a Hawaiian buffet feast. A highlight of any Hawaii trip.

meals.breakfast: Café at the hotel or a nearby spot — try Boots & Kimo's in Kailua for famous macadamia nut pancakes if you're willing to make the drive. Otherwise, a simple hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Chinatown Honolulu — explore the vibrant food stalls and restaurants. Try Fete Hawaii for creative Hawaiian-inspired cuisine or a local dim sum spot. Budget ~$12–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Included in Paradise Cove Luau package — adult tickets ~$115–140, children ~$75–90. Book well in advance as it sells out.

day_by_day.notes: Paradise Cove is located in Ko Olina (~35 min drive west of Honolulu). The luau typically starts at 5:00 PM with check-in at 4:30 PM. Wear comfortable clothing and bring a light layer for the evening breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Beginner Surf Lessons at Waikiki Beach — take a 2-hour group surf lesson with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki. Suitable for all ages, including young children. Most participants stand up on their first day!
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, enjoy free time on Waikiki Beach. Build sandcastles, swim, or simply relax under an umbrella. Walk the famous Kalakaua Avenue and browse the shops at the International Marketplace.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Waikiki Beach, then enjoy a leisurely dinner in the neighborhood. Catch the free weekly Kuhio Beach Hula Show at the Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays at dusk — free admission).

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things on Waikiki — iconic breakfast spot famous for their pancakes with whipped cream. Arrive early to avoid lines. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at a food truck or beachside café near Waikiki — try a shrimp plate or acai bowl. Budget ~$10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — wildly popular, affordable, and delicious. Handmade udon noodles, tempura, and musubi. Budget ~$8–12 per person. Expect a line but it moves fast.

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons typically run ~$40–60 per person for a group lesson. Book through a reputable school like Hans Hedemann Surf School or Aloha Beach Services. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before lessons.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore — stop at the Dole Plantation for a pineapple soft-serve, the famous Pineapple Express train tour, and the world's largest outdoor maze. Fun for the whole family. (~45 min from Waikiki)
day_by_day.afternoon: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa — stroll through the charming surf town of Haleiwa on the North Shore. Sample Hawaii's most beloved shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's, browse local surf shops, and soak up the laid-back North Shore vibe. In summer, the waves are calm — great for swimming at Haleiwa Beach Park.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach Park on the North Shore. Watch the surfers (even in summer, there are some waves) and enjoy the golden hour. Drive back to East Oahu for the night.

meals.breakfast: Café Haleiwa in Haleiwa town — a beloved local breakfast spot with hearty omelets and pancakes. Budget ~$12–18 per person.
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck — a legendary North Shore food truck famous for garlic shrimp plates. Cash only, budget ~$14–16 per plate.
meals.dinner: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa or drive back and dine at Assaggio Italian Restaurant in Hawaii Kai — mid-range Italian with fresh pasta and seafood. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from East Oahu to the North Shore takes about 45–60 minutes. Traffic can be heavy on Friday afternoons heading back — plan to leave the North Shore by 4:00–4:30 PM or stay for sunset and return after 7:00 PM to avoid gridlock.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant experience. Book timed entry tickets online in advance for the USS Arizona Memorial (free, but reserve early). The visitor center, museum exhibits, and the memorial are powerful for older children and adults.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Honolulu and visit the Ala Moana Beach Park — a large, family-friendly beach with calm, protected waters, grassy picnic areas, and lifeguards on duty. Swim, relax, and let the kids play in the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday evening at Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall. Browse local stores, enjoy live entertainment, and have dinner at one of the many dining options. The mall often features free hula performances on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to Pearl Harbor — aim to arrive at Pearl Harbor by 8:00–8:30 AM.
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor has a café on-site for a quick bite, or pack your own snacks. Alternatively, stop at a nearby plate lunch spot on the way back.
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center food options — try Goma Tei Ramen for excellent Japanese ramen (~$15–18) or Yard House for a wider American menu (~$20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor tickets for the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour are free but must be reserved online at recreation.gov — they often book out weeks in advance. The Battleship Missouri, Pacific Aviation Museum, and USS Bowfin have separate admission fees (~$25–30 each). Budget 3–4 hours total for Pearl Harbor.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to Diamond Head Crater — one of Oahu's most iconic hikes with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. The trail is 1.6 miles round trip with some steep sections and stairs. Arrive early (6:00–7:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Reservation required online (~$5 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and enjoy a beach day at Sans Souci Beach (also called Kaimana Beach) near Diamond Head — a quieter, less crowded alternative to Waikiki with calm, clear water and a relaxed local vibe. Perfect for snorkeling and swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special family dinner at a nicer restaurant to celebrate a wonderful trip so far. Head to Waikiki for dinner with an ocean view.

meals.breakfast: Pack granola bars and fruit for the early hike. After the hike, treat yourselves to breakfast at Café Kaila in Market City — famous for fluffy pancakes and creative eggs Benedict. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.lunch: Barefoot Beach Café near Kaimana Beach — casual beachside spot with fish tacos, burgers, and fresh salads. Budget ~$14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Orchids at the Halekulani Hotel — an upscale oceanfront restaurant with exquisite Hawaiian seafood and stunning sunset views. Mid-range splurge night. Budget ~$50–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head reservations can be made at hawaii.goingtocamp.com. Bring water, wear sunscreen, and sturdy shoes. The hike takes about 1–1.5 hours round trip. The crater is located just 10 minutes from the hotel area.

day_by_day.morning: Sea Life Park Hawaii — located near Hanauma Bay, this marine park is perfect for families. Swim with dolphins, watch sea lion shows, see Hawaiian monk seals, penguins, and sea turtles up close. Great for younger children especially.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hanauma Bay area for a final afternoon beach session — swim, snorkel, or simply relax and soak in the beauty of East Oahu. Pack a picnic and enjoy the surroundings near the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise or walk along the Makapu'u Lighthouse Trail for one last golden-hour view of the coastline. The trail is a 2-mile round trip paved path with stunning views of the Windward Coast and offshore islands.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby spot — try Keneke's BBQ in Hawaii Kai for a local Hawaiian breakfast plate with eggs, rice, and spam. Budget ~$10–14 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local grocery store or deli to enjoy at the beach near the hotel.
meals.dinner: Moana Surfrider's Veranda in Waikiki — enjoy afternoon tea-style dining or a sunset dinner on the historic beachfront veranda of the 'First Lady of Waikiki.' Budget ~$30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park admission is ~$40–50 for adults, ~$25–35 for children. Dolphin swim experiences are an additional cost (~$100–200 per person) and must be booked in advance. The park is only 5 minutes from the hotel — very convenient.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow, relaxed breakfast and take one last walk along the beach near the hotel. Collect any last shells, take photos, and soak in the aloha spirit. Pack up and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, stop at a local souvenir shop or the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (open Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday — check if applicable) for last-minute gifts. Alternatively, stop at Longs Drugs or ABC Stores for affordable Hawaii souvenirs. Drive to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — mahalo and aloha! Carry the spirit of Hawaii home with you.

meals.breakfast: One last local breakfast — try Rainbow Drive-In in Honolulu, a legendary local plate lunch institution open since 1961. Try the loco moco (rice, hamburger patty, egg, and gravy) for a true Hawaii farewell. Budget ~$10–14 per person.
meals.lunch: Airport dining or a quick stop at a food truck near the airport. Honolulu Airport has decent dining options including local Hawaiian food.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure, or 2 hours for domestic. Return your rental car before checking in. Consider purchasing fresh pineapple, Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, and Hawaiian sea salt as gifts — all available at the airport duty-free and local stores.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots inside a protected marine sanctuary. Families can swim alongside colorful tropical fish and sea turtles in calm, shallow waters. Reservations are required in advance and an educational video is shown before entry.

experiences.name: Catamaran Sunset Sail off Waikiki
experiences.description: Board a family-friendly catamaran for a 2-hour sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Enjoy views of Diamond Head, spot dolphins and sea turtles, and experience the magic of a Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean. Light snacks and drinks are typically included.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove
experiences.description: Experience an authentic Hawaiian luau on the beach featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and haupia coconut pudding. A wonderful cultural immersion for the whole family right on the oceanfront.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming surf town of Haleiwa on the North Shore and sample Hawaii's most beloved food traditions. Try world-famous shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies — a delicious and affordable family food adventure.

experiences.name: Beginner Surf Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take a 2-hour group surf lesson with certified instructors on the gentle rolling waves of Waikiki, considered one of the best beginner surf spots in the world. Suitable for kids and adults alike, boards and rash guards are provided. Most first-timers stand up on their first lesson!

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Honolulu International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Hanauma Bay Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the scenic East Oahu coastline near the hotel to soak in the first views of the Pacific. Unpack and settle into your premium suite.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the hotel or nearby upscale East Oahu restaurant to ease into Hawaiian time. Enjoy a relaxed sunset from the property's terrace or beach access point.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or light snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments arranged by the boutique hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kona Brewing Company Koko Marina (East Oahu) — fresh local seafood, craft beers, and stunning marina views in a relaxed upscale setting

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance. Ask the concierge to arrange a welcome fruit basket, fresh flower leis, and a briefing on the week's planned activities. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 9 PM local time.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (8:00 AM) to secure entry into this protected marine sanctuary before crowds build. Explore vibrant coral reefs and swim alongside tropical fish, sea turtles, and reef sharks in one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots. Gear rentals and guided orientation included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a poolside or beachside lunch, then enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the boutique stay's private beach area. Optional: book a private paddleboard session through the hotel concierge along the calm East Oahu shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace followed by a premium dinner showcasing Hawaiian regional cuisine.

meals.breakfast: In-room or hotel restaurant breakfast — fresh açaí bowls, tropical fruit platters, Kona coffee, and eggs Benedict with kalua pork
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the hotel — lobster rolls, poke bowls, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roy's Hawaii Kai — legendary Hawaiian Fusion cuisine by Chef Roy Yamaguchi, just minutes from Hanauma Bay. Try the misoyaki butterfish and molten chocolate soufflé.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — confirm with the concierge the night before. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only (required by Hawaii state law). Best snorkeling visibility is in the morning hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury van excursion to Waikiki Beach for Beginner Surf Lessons (2-hour group or private lesson with certified instructors). The gentle rolling waves of Waikiki are ideal for all ages and skill levels. Board rental and instruction included; private lessons can be arranged for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Waikiki's upscale shopping district — browse luxury boutiques at the Royal Hawaiian Center and Kalakaua Avenue. Enjoy shave ice from Waiola Shave Ice (a local institution) and stroll along the iconic Waikiki promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Catamaran Sunset Sail off Waikiki — board a family-friendly premium catamaran for a 2-hour sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Enjoy panoramic views of Diamond Head, complimentary cocktails, and Hawaiian live music as the sun dips into the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — macadamia nut pancakes, fresh papaya, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Duke's Waikiki — iconic oceanfront dining with fresh fish tacos, coconut shrimp, and tropical cocktails right on the beach
meals.dinner: Post-sail dinner at Nobu Honolulu in Waikiki — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion with premium omakase options and fresh Hawaiian seafood

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons and the catamaran sail in advance through the hotel concierge. The catamaran typically departs around 5:00–5:30 PM; confirm timing with the operator. Bring a light layer for the evening sail as ocean breezes can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike to Diamond Head Summit — depart early (7:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail offers breathtaking panoramic views of Waikiki, Honolulu, and the Pacific Ocean from the rim of this iconic volcanic crater. Suitable for families with children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Pali Highway to the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for dramatic windward coast views, then visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum with interactive exhibits perfect for families. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, royal regalia, and a stunning planetarium show.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove — experience an authentic Hawaiian luau on the beach featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a lavish feast of kalua pig, poi, haupia, and tropical cocktails. A spectacular family highlight.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the hike — granola, yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mud Hen Water (Kaimuki neighborhood) — inventive Hawaiian comfort food by Chef Ed Kenney using locally sourced ingredients
meals.dinner: Included in the Paradise Cove Luau package — full traditional Hawaiian feast with open bar

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance reservations and a small entry fee — book online ahead of time. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water for the hike. The luau typically runs 5:00–9:00 PM; arrange private round-trip transportation through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury excursion to the North Shore — depart at 8:00 AM via scenic Kamehameha Highway along the windward coast. Stop at the stunning Kualoa Ranch for a private ATV or horseback riding adventure through lush valleys featured in Jurassic Park and other Hollywood films. Spectacular scenery and family fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa — arrive in the charming surf town of Haleiwa for a guided tasting tour. Sample Hawaii's most beloved shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh garlic shrimp from the famous North Shore shrimp trucks, acai bowls, and local tropical fruit. Browse the eclectic boutiques and surf shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Sunset Beach or Banzai Pipeline — watch the legendary surf breaks of the North Shore in golden hour light. Return to East Oahu via private transfer for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, Portuguese sausage, taro waffles, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: North Shore shrimp plate from Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (a legendary local experience) plus shave ice from Matsumoto's
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vintage Cave Honolulu — one of Hawaii's most exclusive and acclaimed fine dining restaurants, offering a multi-course tasting menu with impeccable wine pairings (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Kualoa Ranch activities must be booked well in advance — request the private family package through your concierge. The North Shore drive is approximately 45–60 minutes from East Oahu. Vintage Cave requires reservations months ahead; confirm before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private snorkeling and marine wildlife boat charter from Kewalo Basin or Hawaii Kai Marina — explore sea caves, lava arches, and pristine reefs along the South Shore. Spot spinner dolphins, green sea turtles, and colorful reef fish with a private naturalist guide. Luxury vessel with onboard refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a luxurious afternoon of relaxation — book a private beach cabana, enjoy the pool, or indulge in spa treatments at the hotel's wellness facility or a nearby luxury spa (Moana Lani Spa at the Moana Surfrider is highly recommended).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace followed by a romantic and family-friendly beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — smoked salmon Benedict, tropical smoothie bowls, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel and enjoyed aboard the private boat charter — charcuterie, fresh sashimi, tropical fruits, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's Fish House (advance reservation required) or equivalent East Oahu fine dining — celebrated for its ultra-fresh catch-of-the-day preparations and stunning oceanfront ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2 weeks in advance. Request the hotel spa to arrange in-room massages as an alternative if preferred. This is a great day to let the family set their own pace after several active days.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Oahu — depart from Honolulu Airport for a breathtaking 45–60 minute aerial tour over Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, the North Shore, Waimea Valley, and the stunning windward coast. An unforgettable luxury experience offering perspectives impossible to see from the ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — tour the USS Arizona Memorial, the Battleship Missouri, and the Pacific Aviation Museum for a deeply moving and educational family experience. Private guided tours available for a more immersive and personalized visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a special evening — enjoy the free Friday and Saturday Royal Hawaiian Band concert at Iolani Palace grounds (seasonal), then head to a world-class dinner in Honolulu.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the helicopter tour — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award-winning local institution) — authentic Hawaiian plate lunches including pipikaula short ribs and lomi salmon
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Pig and the Lady (Chinatown, Honolulu) — acclaimed modern Vietnamese-Hawaiian cuisine with inventive cocktails and a vibrant atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours should be booked weeks in advance; Blue Hawaiian Helicopters and Sunshine Helicopters are top-rated operators. Pearl Harbor requires timed entry passes — book online well ahead. The memorial is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lush Waimea Valley on Oahu's North Shore — a sacred botanical garden and nature preserve featuring over 5,000 tropical plant species, peacocks roaming freely, and a stunning 45-foot waterfall at the end of a gentle 1.5-mile walk. Perfect for families and nature lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Shark's Cove on the North Shore for tide pool exploration and snorkeling in the natural lava rock pools (calm in summer months). Afterward, visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in La'ie for an immersive afternoon exploring the cultures of Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand through interactive village experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Polynesian Cultural Center's acclaimed 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a spectacular production featuring over 100 performers, dramatic fire effects, and stunning Polynesian choreography. Dinner package available at the center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — loco moco (a Hawaiian classic: rice, hamburger patty, fried egg, and gravy), fresh tropical juice, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Polynesian Cultural Center's Gateway Restaurant — featuring a Hawaiian buffet with island-inspired dishes
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a premium all-you-can-eat Hawaiian feast paired with the evening show

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from East Oahu (about 1 hour drive). Book the evening show and dinner package in advance. The center is operated by Brigham Young University–Hawaii and is closed on Sundays — confirm current operating days before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking excursion from Kailua Beach on the windward coast — paddle through the calm turquoise waters to the uninhabited Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes'), a protected seabird sanctuary with stunning white sand beaches. A truly exclusive and serene experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Kailua — browse its eclectic boutiques, art galleries, and local shops. Visit Lanikai Beach, consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the world, for a relaxing afternoon swim in the crystal-clear calm water.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration — return to the hotel for a private beachside dinner arranged by the concierge, featuring a custom menu prepared by a private chef with fresh local ingredients, a bonfire, and traditional Hawaiian music.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-kayak breakfast at the hotel — energy bars, bananas, and coffee, followed by a full brunch post-kayak
meals.lunch: Brunch/lunch at Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for its red velvet pancakes, guava chiffon pancakes, and loco moco. A beloved local institution.
meals.dinner: Private chef beachside dinner at the hotel — curated 4-course menu featuring fresh Hawaiian catch, locally grown produce, and premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayaking excursion through Kailua Beach Adventures or a similar reputable outfitter. Arrange the private chef dinner through the hotel concierge at least 3 days in advance. Kailua is approximately 20 minutes from Hanauma Bay via the Pali Highway.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a long, relaxed breakfast at the hotel, take one last swim at Hanauma Bay or the hotel's private beach, and soak in the final moments of paradise. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Checkout and last-minute souvenir shopping at nearby Koko Marina Shopping Center or a quick stop at a local farmers' market for Hawaiian coffee, macadamia nuts, and artisan goods to bring home. Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the aloha spirit home with memories of 10 extraordinary days in Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — a full spread of Hawaiian favorites: poi waffles, fresh papaya with lime, smoked fish, tropical smoothies, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snacks at Koko Marina or airport dining — Island Vintage Coffee at the Honolulu Airport is an excellent option for acai bowls and coffee before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange a lei farewell ceremony — a beautiful Hawaiian tradition. Request the hotel to prepare a gourmet snack bag for the journey home. Confirm all airport transfers the night before.
